task.title: outfeed-core: declare an inference port so the edge to sawhorse-core burns

acceptance_criteria:
DESIGN DECISION NEEDED 2026-11-06, before any code. I started this and stopped: the seam is not a leaf module like GB-284's was, and the two options below differ architecturally rather than cosmetically.

THE FACTS. plan_release, apply_release, release_repo, release_repo_with_plan, plan_suite_releases, execute_suite_plan and the suite-wave entry all live INSIDE outfeed-core, and the per-repo loops live there too (suite_waves/entry.rs calls release_repo per repo). So enrichment cannot be a parameter passed by the CLI: the CLI does not own the loop that needs it. ReleaseOpts is #[derive(Debug, Clone)] and constructed field-by-field at every call site, so an injected port also breaks every constructor unless added with ..Default::default().

What is already clean and worth keeping: find_storypole_root is a bare directory walk that touches no storypole type and belongs in core wherever else moves; and task_summaries is already &[(String, String, String)], so no storypole type crosses the seam today. Only the fetching and synthesizing calls carry the dependency.

OPTION A - port on ReleaseOpts. Add Arc<dyn ReleaseEnrichment> with an async notes method returning a boxed future (dyn-safe without a new dependency), summaries and record_release as sync methods, and a Default no-op impl so library callers are unaffected. Touches ~5 signatures, 3 impls, 2 adapter modules in outfeed-cli and outfeed-mcp. Mechanical, no behavior change, but it is a trait object that exists only to avoid moving code.

OPTION B - move the orchestrator out of core. release/, suite_plan/ and suite_waves/ move to an integrator-level crate that may legitimately depend on storypole and sawhorse; outfeed-core keeps planning, applying, semver and deterministic changelog formatting. The edges become structurally impossible rather than injected, and core loses two dependencies permanently.

RECOMMENDATION: B, and not only for purity. Under A, outfeed-core still names the other products' capabilities, so the allowlist entry would keep existing in a different costume - the gate would pass while the coupling survives, which is the failure mode this whole burn-down exists to kill. B is the multi-hour job: it moves release_all, suite waves, the CLI and the MCP dispatch, and it needs the ReleaseOpts split.

Not started deliberately. A half-moved orchestrator leaves outfeed unbuildable, and I would rather hand over a decision than a broken crate.

CONFIRMED 2026-11-06, and it makes Option B cheaper than my estimate above: sawhorse_core and storypole_core are referenced ONLY from synthesis.rs and storypole.rs inside outfeed-core. There is no second use anywhere in the crate - grep for either name across outfeed-core/src excluding those two files returns nothing. So Option B is a move of three directories plus those two modules; no scattered call sites need rewriting, and the two manifest lines (storypole-core, sawhorse-core) come out with nothing to untangle behind them.

Revised estimate for B: move release/, suite_plan/, suite_waves/ and the two integration modules to an integrator-level crate; outfeed-core keeps engine/, semver, manifest, changelog, git. Signatures move with their callers, so the churn is the CLI and MCP entry points plus the crate manifest.

DONE 2026-11-06, commit 146fff9 (outfeed). Release orchestration moved above the core; both edges burned by relocation rather than injection.

outfeed-core no longer depends on storypole-core or sawhorse-core - both lines are gone from its manifest - and neither name appears anywhere in its source. The orchestrator (release/, suite_plan/, suite_waves/, suite_exec.rs, storypole.rs, synthesis.rs, plus their tests) lives in outfeed-mcp, which outfeed-cli already depends on, so one copy serves the binary and the MCP surface and no integrator-to-integrator edge was created.

The seam needed a real change, not just a file move: synthesize_release_notes needs the target version, which only the planner computes, so plan_release split into plan_basis (pure: commits, referenced tickets, bump classification, target version) and finish_plan (manifest and changelog diffs). The integrator gathers notes between the two. plan_release survives as the one-call form for callers passing no notes.

One behavior improved rather than merely preserved: the release ticket used to be created fire-and-forget inside apply_release, from the core, with errors swallowed by `if let Ok`. The orchestrator now records it after a successful apply and reports either the ticket key or that no backlog was found. A silent failure became a reported one.

Layers: lateral allowlist 3 -> 1, and the survivor is dado-core -> miter-polyglot, which is MTR-22's edge. Downward 150, verdict clean.

Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean, 91 tests green, docs 9 present 0 drifted, 11/11 lockfiles fresh.

acceptance_criteria:
PLACEMENT CORRECTED 2026-11-06, commit 4a95355 (outfeed) + a6f156c (miter).

The work in 146fff9 was right; where it landed was wrong. Release orchestration was moved into outfeed-mcp because outfeed-cli already depended on it - a reason of convenience. -mcp is the MCP protocol surface, and hosting a release orchestrator there put real logic in the wrong layer.

Release orchestration now lives in its own package, crates/outfeed-orchestrator, following miter's shape of focused subcrates. outfeed-core plans and applies one repository; outfeed-orchestrator composes the suite; outfeed-cli and outfeed-mcp consume it and hold none of it. outfeed-mcp is a thin MCP adapter again.

The module named storypole became backlog: outfeed should not own a module named after another product, and the name also produced a phantom edge (outfeed_orchestrator::storypole read as a dependency on the storypole facade) that survived a re-index.

Classification went to ORCHESTRATORS in miter with the reasoning recorded: cutting a suite release is composing, and the crate exists as its own package precisely so the core need not name any of that. Its edges to storypole-core and sawhorse-core are the composition, so they are Downward, not Lateral. Layers still show 1 lateral edge - dado-core -> miter-polyglot, blocked on MTR-22 - with downward rising 150 -> 154.
